name: Wang Bao 王褒 (Northern Zhou)
bio: Wang Bao (c. 513-576), courtesy name Ziyuan, was a courtier and poet of the Liang dynasty. When Liang Jiangling fell to the Western Wei in 554 he was taken north to Chang'an, where he served the Western Wei and then the Northern Zhou, and he is remembered for frontier poems written in exile.

He is not the Western Han writer Wang Bao, author of the Chuci piece Jiu huai; the two share a name and nothing else. The texts here are from zh.wikisource, drawn from the Wang sikong ji and the Gushi yuan.

poems.title: 關山篇 (Guanshan pian)
poems.author: Wang Bao 王褒 (Northern Zhou)
poems.text:
從軍出隴阪，
驅馬度關山。
關山恒掩藹，
髙峯白雲外。
遥望秦川水，
千里長如帶。
好勇自秦中，
意氣多豪雄。
少年便習戰，
十四已從戎。
遼水深難渡，
榆關斷未通。

poems.title: 渡河北 (Du He bei)
poems.author: Wang Bao 王褒 (Northern Zhou)
poems.text:
秋風吹木葉，
還似洞庭波。
常山臨代郡，
亭障繞黃河。
心悲異方樂，
腸斷隴頭歌。
薄暮臨征馬，
失道北山阿。
